## 🎨 Design

- New UI typeface: the whole interface is set in Sansation, self-hosted with no runtime call to Google. The wordmark stays in Bitter.
- Refreshed hero copy: a lighter tagline over a single line, "Encrypted · auto-deleted · no tracking · no account · no bullshit", translated into all 26 languages.
- Consistent download page: the brand sits at the top and links home, and the share card is crowned with just the logo, the same as on the main page.
- A bigger logo and more breathing room on the home page.
- Reworked upload options panel: expiry is an on/off toggle like the download limit (off means the share never expires). The order is expiry, download limit, password. The divider above the upload button is gone.
- "Feather-light" wording in the short description, in the GitHub repo description, the README, the Unraid template and the templates-repo card.

## ⚡ Improved

- A much leaner image that behaves exactly the same: the published container is about 58% smaller (203 MB down to 85 MB compressed). The runtime ships Next's `output: "standalone"` build, which holds only the trace-pruned server and about 24 MB of `node_modules` (down from about 498 MB) instead of the full dependency tree. Pulls are faster and the footprint is smaller. Ports, the `/data` volume and the configuration stay the same, so there's nothing to change on upgrade. The custom server mounts a tus handler next to Next and can't use Next's generated `server.js`, so it hands Next the pre-resolved config (`__NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE_CONFIG`) and the standalone runtime starts without the pruned webpack machinery.
- The image push waits for a boot smoke test: CI builds the image, starts it and requires it to actually serve a request, on both `amd64` and `arm64`, before it publishes `:latest`. A build that compiles but can't start never reaches the published tag.
- Self-hosting docs and template: the README has a new "Security & Privacy" section. The Unraid template pre-fills a `BASE_URL` placeholder and explains that `APP_LOGO` accepts a URL or a `data:` URI, so a custom logo needs no hosting.

## 🐛 Fixed

- The light/dark toggle needed two clicks for the first switch. One click does it now.
- The image and PDF preview sometimes never appeared on the download page. Three things were behind it, and all three are fixed:
  - When the browser sent no `filetype` with the tus upload, the database stored no MIME type, so the page decided the file couldn't be previewed and never drew the preview box. The client now infers the content type from the revealed filename's extension as a fallback (`lib/mime.ts`), and the server does the same for the inline request and its `Content-Type`. Older files without a stored MIME type now preview correctly without a re-upload.
  - Behind some reverse proxies the auth cookie didn't reliably reach the image request. The per-file link key, which is already in the URL fragment, is now also passed as `?k=` on the `?inline=1` path for unlimited shares, so the preview no longer depends on the cookie.
  - The preview frame collapsed to zero height when loading failed. It now has a `minHeight` and flexbox centering, so the box is always visible.
- `BASE_URL` now applies to generated share links (#1). The link was built from the browser's `window.location.origin`, so behind a reverse proxy it used the internal address instead of your public domain. `BASE_URL` is now resolved on the server and passed to the client through `ServerConfigProvider` (the same pattern as `BrandingProvider`). The link falls back to the browser's address only when `BASE_URL` is unset.
- Lint CI is green again: the obsolete `XML Template Lint` job is gone. The Unraid template lives in the central templates repo and is validated there, so the job kept failing on files that no longer exist here.
- The language flag and the light/dark toggle sit in the same spot on every page. They were placed inside each page's content container, and the download page uses a narrower container than the upload page, so on wide screens they landed in different places. Both are now pinned to the top-right corner of the viewport.

## 🌐 Translations

- The "Download options" heading (`settings.title`) replaces "Share options" in all 26 languages.
- German grammar: the expiry labels read "7 Tagen" and "30 Tagen" (dative case).
